subject: chemistry
title: Proton Pulsar: Bronsted-Lowry and pH
welcome_lead: Define acids and bases and compute pH from concentration.
meta_desc: A-Level chemistry adventure on Bronsted-Lowry acids, bases and pH.
final_note: You now read pH like a chemical clock.

concepts.def: Acid <-> base differs by one H+.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Strong acids fully dissociate: HCl -> H+ + Cl-. So [H+] = [acid].

pH = -log10[H+]. Example: 0.01 mol/dm3 HCl -> pH = 2. Diprotic: 0.01 mol/dm3 H2SO4 -> [H+]=0.02 -> pH ≈ 1.7.

NaOH -> Na+ + OH-. Use Kw: [H+] = Kw/[OH-].

Example: 0.1 mol/dm3 NaOH gives [H+]=1e-13, pH = 13.

NH3 + H2O <-> NH4+ + OH-. Conjugate pairs: NH3/NH4+ and H2O/OH-.

Strong acid has weak conjugate base; weak acid has stronger conjugate base. Water is amphiprotic.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a strong acid and a concentrated acid?
options: A strong acid fully dissociates in water; a concentrated acid has a high amount of acid per volume — these are independent properties.
Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.
A strong acid is one that has been heated to higher temperature.
Strong and concentrated mean the same thing for acids.

mcqs.q: How does a buffer maintain its pH when small amounts of acid are added?
options: A buffer prevents any H+ ions from being added to the solution at all.
A buffer destroys added acid by changing it into water vapour.
The conjugate base in the buffer reacts with added H+ to remove it, keeping pH nearly constant.
Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.

mcqs.q: Where is almost all the mass of an atom located?
options: Electrons contribute significantly to the mass of an atom.
Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.
A strong acid is one that has been heated to higher temperature.
In the nucleus, made up of protons and neutrons.
